The RB strategy (12) is an effective method for adjusting the penalty parameter, which describes the convergence properties of ADMM [22]. Combined with the spectral penalty parameter scheme (30), the RB strategy inspires us that if ‖ r k ‖ 2 > ‖ d k ‖ 2 , then in the next iteration, a small spectral gradient step size is reasonable (corresponding to a large regularization parameter τ k +1 ); otherwise, a large spectral gradient step size (corresponding to a small regularization parameter τ k +1 ) is selected when ‖ r k ‖ 2 < ‖ d k ‖ 2 . texts.orig: where matrix R m × n is the historical returns of asset i on its i -th column over m observation periods, see [7]. The observation data contained in this matrix is used to estimate two important parameters in MV model: expected return and covariance matrix. If the number of the chosen observations m is small compared to the number of assets, then the sample covariance matrix becomes ill-conditioned, one suffers from the over-fitting problem [12, 3]. In this case, a high regularization promotes the sparsity of the solutions and mitigates over-fitting. On the other hand, if the number of samples is large enough, then the model obtained is truth and a small amount of regularization is reasonable. Based on these, we regard 1 m as a factor of the initial regularization parameter λ 0 .
